messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] can't read.cross because of missing marker positions?
parts:
You need to just delete that third row with blanks. Either include positions for all markers or leave that row off.

Also, the 'alleles' argument expects single-letter codes, so you might just use alleles=c("N", "O"). The two-letter codes might work, but I'm not sure.

karl


On Aug 3, 2012, at 3:03 PM, rmreynol wrote:

> Hi all,
>
> I suspect that I'm doing something silly that is causing read.cross not to function properly. Can you help? I am making a linkage map for a RIL population using 15K markers (this will likely be reduced to ~4K after quality control filtering). I have made a less detailed linkage map using 2K markers from this population previously, and all rqtl commands worked well. As far as I can tell, I've formatted these new data identically, using the BC input format. However, when I enter the command:
>
> > creMap <- read.cross(format = "csv", file = "BC1_8-2-12.csv", na.strings = c("-"), genotypes=c("A", "B"), alleles=c("NY", "OH"), estimate.map = FALSE)
>
> I get the error message:
>
> Error in read.cross.csv(dir, file, na.strings, genotypes, estimate.map, :
> There are missing marker positions.
> In particular, we see these values: ""
>
> I suspect the issue is with the formatting of the data file, which I have attached. I am using the U of Oregon computing cloud, ACCIS, which has R 2.14.2 and my local machine is a Mac with OS X Lion 10.7.4. I am working with R through my terminal. Please let me know if you need further information.
>
> Any ideas?
> Rose
